name: Request Router
description: The central decision-maker for each request. Given a TaskRequest: (1) checks budget via Budget Manager, (2) gets current phase and confidence via Confidence Engine, (3) gets sampling decision via Sampling Scheduler, (4) routes accordingly based on the phase × sampling × budget matrix. Phase 1: send to remote only, store response as training example. Phase 2 (coaching sample): send to both local and remote, evaluate pair, store training example, return remote response to caller. Phase 2 (non-coaching): send to both, return remote response. Phase 3 (coaching sample): send to both, evaluate pair, return local response to caller (remote is for monitoring). Phase 3 (non-coaching): send to local only, return local response. Fallback: if local model fails, fall back to remote (counts against budget). If budget exhausted, serve degraded response from local only or return degraded result. Logs every routing decision to audit log with full context (phase, confidence, sampling decision, intended/actual route, cost, latency). All collaborators are injected via constructor as typing.Protocol interfaces. Uses asyncio.gather for dual-send concurrency. Never exceeds budget — budget enforcement is hard.

functions.name: route
functions.description: Route a single task request through the phase × sampling × budget decision matrix. This is the sole public method of RequestRouter. It coordinates all collaborators: checks budget, gets phase/confidence, gets sampling decision, executes the appropriate routing action, collects training data, logs the audit entry, and returns the complete result. Uses asyncio.gather for dual-send scenarios. Handles all fallback and degradation paths. Never raises for recoverable failures — all degraded outcomes are represented in the return type.

inputs.name: request
inputs.description: The inbound task request to be routed.

preconditions: request.request_id is a valid non-empty string
request.timestamp_utc is a valid ISO 8601 UTC timestamp
All collaborators (BudgetManager, ConfidenceEngine, SamplingScheduler, LocalModelBackend, RemoteModelBackend, TrainingDataCollector, AuditLogger) have been injected and are operational
RouterConfig has been validated at construction time
postconditions: Returned RoutingResult.request_id == request.request_id
Returned RoutingResult.response contains a valid ModelResponse with non-empty content
Returned RoutingResult.intended_action reflects the action computed from the decision matrix before execution
Returned RoutingResult.actual_action reflects what actually happened (may differ from intended due to fallback)
If actual_action != intended_action, then is_fallback == True
If is_fallback == True, actual_action is LOCAL_FALLBACK_TO_REMOTE
If is_degraded == True, the response came from local-only when local quality may be insufficient
total_cost_usd == sum of costs of all model calls made (local cost is 0 or near-0, remote cost > 0)
BudgetManager.record_spend() has been called with total_cost_usd for this request
A RoutingAuditEntry has been submitted to AuditLogger (fire-and-forget, failure does not affect result)
If the routing action involved a remote response in Phase 1 or Phase 2, a TrainingExample of type REMOTE_RESPONSE_EXAMPLE was submitted to TrainingDataCollector
If the routing action was a dual-send and both backends succeeded, a TrainingExample of type COACHING_EVALUATION_PAIR was submitted to TrainingDataCollector
Budget is never exceeded — if budget was exhausted before routing, no remote call is made
side_effects: Calls remote model API (network call, incurs cost)
Calls local model server (network call to local inference server)
Records spend against budget via BudgetManager
Emits audit log entry via AuditLogger

structured_side_effects.description: Sends prompt to remote API (e.g., Claude, GPT) when routing action requires remote. Incurs monetary cost.
Sends prompt to local model inference server when routing action requires local.
Records the cost of remote API calls against the budget. Mutates budget state.
Persists training example data from remote responses in Phase 1 and Phase 2.
Persists coaching evaluation pair when both backends succeed in a dual-send scenario.
Emits a structured RoutingAuditEntry as JSON for the machine-readable audit trail. Fire-and-forget.

functions.name: compute_routing_action
functions.description: Pure function that computes the intended RoutingAction from the current phase, coaching sample status, and budget availability. Implements the phase × sampling × budget decision matrix using match/case for exhaustive branch coverage. This is a deterministic, side-effect-free computation extracted for testability. Decision matrix: Phase 1 + budget available → REMOTE_ONLY. Phase 1 + budget exhausted → LOCAL_ONLY (degraded). Phase 2 + coaching sample + budget available → BOTH_RETURN_REMOTE. Phase 2 + not coaching sample + budget available → BOTH_RETURN_REMOTE. Phase 2 + budget exhausted → LOCAL_ONLY (degraded). Phase 3 + coaching sample + budget available → BOTH_RETURN_LOCAL. Phase 3 + not coaching sample → LOCAL_ONLY. Phase 3 + coaching sample + budget exhausted → LOCAL_ONLY (degraded, skips coaching).

inputs.name: phase
inputs.description: Current phase from the Confidence Engine.

inputs.name: is_coaching_sample
inputs.description: Whether the Sampling Scheduler selected this request for coaching.

inputs.name: budget_available
inputs.description: Whether there is sufficient budget remaining for a remote API call.

preconditions: phase is a valid Phase enum value
postconditions: Return value is always a valid RoutingAction enum member
If budget_available is False, return value is never REMOTE_ONLY, BOTH_RETURN_REMOTE, or BOTH_RETURN_LOCAL
If phase is PHASE_1 and budget_available is True, return value is REMOTE_ONLY
If phase is PHASE_3 and is_coaching_sample is False, return value is LOCAL_ONLY regardless of budget
The function is deterministic: same inputs always produce the same output

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function with no side effects.

functions.name: execute_dual_send
functions.description: Execute a dual-send to both local and remote backends concurrently using asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True). Handles all four outcome combinations (both succeed, local fails/remote succeeds, local succeeds/remote fails, both fail) explicitly. Returns the outcome enum and both responses (or None for failed backends). This method does NOT perform fallback — it reports what happened. The caller decides how to handle each outcome.

inputs.name: request
inputs.description: The task request to send to both backends.

error_cases.name: timeout_exceeded
error_cases.condition: asyncio.gather itself times out or is cancelled (not individual backend timeouts, which are handled as failures)

preconditions: LocalModelBackend and RemoteModelBackend are injected and reachable (though individual calls may still fail)
postconditions: Returned DualSendResult.outcome accurately reflects which backends succeeded and failed
If outcome is BOTH_SUCCEEDED, both local_response and remote_response are non-None
If outcome is LOCAL_FAILED_REMOTE_SUCCEEDED, local_response is None and remote_response is non-None
If outcome is LOCAL_SUCCEEDED_REMOTE_FAILED, local_response is non-None and remote_response is None
If outcome is BOTH_FAILED, both local_response and remote_response are None
local_error is non-empty if and only if local backend failed
remote_error is non-empty if and only if remote backend failed
Both backends were called concurrently (not sequentially)

structured_side_effects.description: Concurrent call to remote model backend.
Concurrent call to local model backend.

functions.name: build_audit_entry
functions.description: Build a complete RoutingAuditEntry from the request, routing decision, and execution result. Pure function that assembles the audit record for structured logging. Called after execution completes (or fails) to capture full context.

inputs.name: decision
inputs.description: The pre-execution routing decision with phase, sampling, and budget context.

inputs.name: error_detail
inputs.description: Error detail if any backend failed or fallback occurred.

preconditions: request, decision, and result are valid and internally consistent (same request_id)
postconditions: Returned RoutingAuditEntry.request_id == request.request_id
All fields of the audit entry are populated from the corresponding input fields
timestamp_utc is set to the current UTC time at the moment of building

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function with no side effects.

invariants: Budget is never exceeded — if budget is exhausted, remote calls are not made and the result is degraded
Every call to route() produces exactly one RoutingAuditEntry logged via AuditLogger, regardless of success or failure
Audit logging failures are captured but never block or delay the response to the caller
Local model failures in dual-send or local-only scenarios trigger fallback to remote only if budget allows
The intended_action and actual_action in RoutingResult always reflect ground truth of what was planned vs executed
Training data is collected for every successful remote response in Phase 1 and Phase 2
Coaching pairs are collected for every dual-send scenario where both backends succeed
No global state — all state flows through explicit parameters or injected dependencies
RoutingAction is computed deterministically from (phase, is_coaching_sample, budget_available) inputs
Concurrency: dual-send uses asyncio.gather(return_exceptions=True) and all 4 outcome combinations are handled explicitly
